fixes.explanation: Foreign cases never come up here. Paul asks if they aren't “…competent to judge trivial cases?” The comparison is the world-sized job against small everyday disputes, not home against far away. Trivial is the word he uses.

Angels it is. Paul asks, “Do you not know that we will judge angels?” Then he adds, “How much more the things of this life!” If you'll be doing that, a squabble over everyday stuff is a pretty light load, friend.

Prophets aren't named in these verses. After saying the saints will judge the world, Paul asks, “Do you not know that we will judge angels?” Angels are the answer. And he follows it with, “How much more the things of this life!”
Paul never mentions kings of Israel here. He says, “Do you not know that we will judge angels?” Angels are who he names. Then he finishes with, “How much more the things of this life!”

Paul says nothing about buildings or room sizes. What he asks is, “Is there really no one among you wise enough to arbitrate between his brothers?” His question is about a wise person among them. A bigger room has nothing to do with it, friend.

Prophets don't show up in this verse. Paul says it happens “…in front of unbelievers!” That's the sting: a dispute between brothers is being taken before people who don't believe. He says it with an exclamation point, so I think it really bothers him.

Yes, that's the hard one. Paul asks, “Why not rather be wronged? Why not rather be cheated?” It's tough to hear. I think letting something go instead of taking it to court is one of the hardest things there is, and that's the question he asks.

Paul doesn't offer to come and decide anything here. His question is, “Why not rather be wronged? Why not rather be cheated?” The hard thing he names is being willing to be wronged. Earlier he asks if someone wise among them can arbitrate (1 Corinthians 6:5), but he never says it should be him.

Quiet and distant isn't the picture Paul paints. He says, “Instead, you yourselves cheat and do wrong, even against your own brothers!” The ones doing the cheating and wronging are the Corinthians themselves. So the answer is the cheating and wronging.
